paragraph: Single-family is the engine in Rutherford, with 53 sales over six months at a median of $850,000 and a median of 17 days on market. Nearly 57 percent sold above list, but the sale-to-list ratio of 1.007 says those overages are modest. Call it competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes move quickly, and the range from $530,000 to $1,725,000 is wide enough that the median is the better guide than the average. The monthly series shows volume building the way it normally does, 9 closings in May, 17 in June, 12 in July, while the median eased from $999,999 in May to $837,500 in July. That is a mix shift toward smaller homes on heavier volume, not a value drop. Multi-family is a real category here with 10 sales at a median of $940,000, though the 50-day median days on market says those buyers take their time. Condos and townhouses are the softer tier, 12 sales at a median of $422,500 with a ratio slightly under list and about 40 days on market, so buyers have some room to negotiate. Co-ops are thin at 6 sales and a median of $203,250, and they carry board approval and financing restrictions that not every buyer is aware of going in. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a multi-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
